source: Deletang et al. (2024) Language Modeling Is Compression (ICLR)
finding: A language model plus arithmetic coding is a lossless compressor, so prediction loss is a code length (a computable stand-in for Kolmogorov complexity). Text-trained models also compress images and audio.
numbers: Chinchilla 70B compresses ImageNet patches to 43.4% and LibriSpeech to 16.4% of raw size, vs PNG 58.5% and FLAC 30.3%. enwik9 raw rates: Chinchilla 70B 8.3%, Llama 2 7B 8.9%, gzip 32.3%, LZMA2 23.0%.
limits: Raw rate ignores model size. Adjusted for parameter bytes (two-part code), Chinchilla 70B is 21.9% on enwik9 and over 100% on images and audio in the table. Transformers trained from scratch on enwik8 overfit their modality.
agent_relevance: A model's log-loss is a usable stand-in for description length; the cost of the model itself must be counted or the comparison is unfair (two-part code).

source: Deletang et al. (2024) Language Modeling Is Compression (ICLR)
finding: Any compressor, even gzip, can be turned into a conditional generative model, so compression and prediction are equivalent in both directions.
numbers: Offline adjusted rates of gzip and LZMA2 on a 38M-parameter Transformer: 92.2% and 89.1% (barely any gain).
limits: Generation quality from gzip is low; the point is the equivalence, not a usable generator.
agent_relevance: A cheap compressor gives a crude, model-free complexity measure for agent traces.

source: Huang et al. (2024) Compression Represents Intelligence Linearly (COLM)
finding: Across 31 public LLMs and 12 benchmarks, average benchmark score is almost linear in bits per character on external text.
numbers: Pearson about -0.95 per domain (knowledge, coding, math reasoning); overall -0.93 with RMSE 3.1%.
quote: LLMs' intelligence almost linearly correlates with their ability to compress external text corpora.
limits: Correlation across models, not within one model; the corpus must be fresh to avoid contamination; base models only.
agent_relevance: Compression of fresh text is a label-free quality probe, but it is a model-level metric and does not tell an agent which of two rules to pick.

source: Yoran et al. (2025) The Kolmogorov Test: Compression by Code Generation (ICLR)
finding: Benchmark: give the model a sequence, ask for the shortest program that outputs it. Flagship LLMs fail often.
numbers: Sequences of length 128. GPT4-O fails to reproduce the sequence about 40% of the time on natural data and 55% on synthetic; Llama-3.1-405B fails more than 78% and 65%. Accuracy GPT4-O: audio-16bit 35.6, text 6.5, synthetic 33.3; Llama-405B: 18.0, 9.6, 18.0.
limits: Every prompted model has Precision above 1.0: correct programs are longer than the gzip output. Natural data has no known shortest program.
agent_relevance: Finding even a correct short rule is hard for LLMs; a shortest-rule selector must verify programs by execution, not trust the model.

source: Yoran et al. (2025) The Kolmogorov Test (ICLR)
finding: Training on synthetic program-sequence pairs lifts synthetic results strongly but transfers poorly to real data.
numbers: SeqCoder-1.5B accuracy: audio-16bit 69.5, audio-MFCC 83.8, DNA 50.3, text 54.2, synthetic 44.7. Larger SeqCoder reaches CompressionRate 0.38 on 1MB synthetic data, beating gzip and LMIC. Paper text: near-zero performance on natural sequences for the synthetic-trained models.
limits: The table layout in the extracted text is partly garbled, so the per-modality SeqCoder numbers are read from the first row only. A uniform prior over the authors' DSL beat gzip.
agent_relevance: The prior over the rule language drives compression; a prior learned in the wrong domain does not help.

source: Yoran et al. (2025) The Kolmogorov Test (ICLR)
finding: Prompt and scaffold effects: chain-of-thought barely helps; execution feedback helps a little.
numbers: CoT changed accuracy by -1.3 (Llama 8B) and -5.1 (Llama 70B) points on average, +2.1 for Llama-405B. o1-mini was similar to GPT4-O. Inline execution feedback gave modest gains.
limits: Prompted-only comparisons; no search or RL on real data.
agent_relevance: Reasoning text adds little for finding shorter rules; program-and-check loops need real search.

source: Yoran et al. (2025) The Kolmogorov Test (ICLR)
finding: Failure modes: programs that are too simple (do not reproduce the data) or too complicated (copy the data inside code).
numbers: In more than 30% of failures models try to repeat the input in a complicated way. SeqCoder-1.5B trained on 10K examples: more than 99% of programs err within the first 16 characters; at 100K and 1M examples, 93.5% and 88.7%.
limits: Error analysis by the authors on audio sequences of length 128.
agent_relevance: Always compare against the trivial 'print the data' program (the REPEAT baseline).

source: Grau-Moya et al. (2024) Learning Universal Predictors
finding: Meta-training LSTMs and Transformers on data from random universal Turing machine programs approximates Solomonoff induction; larger models predict better, and sequences from longer programs are harder.
numbers: Cumulative regret falls as model size goes S, M, L; best in-distribution model is Transformer-L; regret rises with the length of the generating program.
limits: Small scale and short sequences; UTM sampling only approximates the universal prior. Exact transfer figures not recorded here.
agent_relevance: Supports 'shorter program means easier sequence'; weak direct use for a scaffold.

source: Grau-Moya et al. (2024) Learning Universal Predictors
finding: Networks trained on UTM data transfer to other tasks, including variable-order Markov sources and Chomsky-hierarchy tasks.
numbers: Paper reports large LSTMs and Transformers trained on UTM data match the optimal predictor on variable-order Markov sources.
limits: Stated at the level of the paper's own summary; I did not record per-task numbers.
agent_relevance: A prior learned from many short programs acts as a reusable simplicity bias.

source: Elmoznino et al. (2025) In-Context Learning and Occam's Razor (ICML)
finding: Next-token loss in an in-context learner equals prequential code length, an upper bound on K(D); so ICL implicitly pays for training error plus model complexity.
numbers: Prequential ICL generalizes better than train-risk ICL at short context (example context length 15) on linear regression, sinusoid regression and Mastermind; the gap grows with task difficulty and vanishes at long context. An SGD-fitted MLP is worse at low data but can win at large data (Mastermind).
limits: Architecture matters: only the Transformer without bottleneck did well on Mastermind; state-space models beat it on HMM. Pretrained LLMs still struggle to minimize prequential code length on novel tasks.
agent_relevance: With few examples, in-context learning favors simple rules; with many examples that pressure disappears.

source: Li et al. (2025) Understanding is Compression (LMCompress)
finding: Arithmetic coding with generative models (image GPT, LoRA-tuned Llama3-8B) beats classical lossless compressors on images, audio, video and text.
numbers: About double the ratio of JPEG-XL (images), FLAC (audio) and H.264 (video); text ratio almost triples the best traditional method (abstract says quadruple bz2). Domain tuning of Llama3-8B raised ratio by 8.5% (MeDAL) and 38.4% (Pile of Law).
limits: Authors' own system; 'understanding implies compression' is an interpretation; decoding needs the large model.
agent_relevance: Domain-conditioned priors compress better, so a rule scorer should be conditioned on the task domain.

source: Jiang et al. (2023) Low-Resource Text Classification: A Parameter-Free Classification Method with Compressors (ACL Findings)
finding: gzip-based normalized compression distance (a Kolmogorov approximation) with kNN is competitive with neural classifiers, with no training.
numbers: gzip test accuracy: AGNews 0.937, DBpedia 0.970, YahooAnswers 0.638, 20News 0.685, Ohsumed 0.521, R8 0.954, R52 0.896. Average of all baseline models: AGNews 0.901, YahooAnswers 0.726.
quote: outperforms BERT on all five OOD datasets
limits: Later shown inflated by tie-breaking (see Opitz). Weak on very large sets such as YahooAnswers.
agent_relevance: Compression distance is cheap and training-free, but check evaluation details before trusting it.

source: Opitz (2023) Gzip versus bag-of-words for text classification
finding: Partial failed replication: the gzip-kNN scores used optimistic tie-breaking; with fair random tie-breaking accuracy drops, and simple bag-of-words distance does as well or better.
numbers: Realistic accuracy fell by up to 9 points on average. With K=2, bag-of-words distance beat gzip by +1.4 points on average and won on 6 of 7 datasets (K=1: +1.1). A trained linear bag-of-words model nearly matched BERT.
limits: Seven datasets; one (DFilipino) has duplicated train and test text and is excluded from means.
agent_relevance: Compression-as-classifier claims need a bug-checked baseline; simple feature baselines can equal them.

source: Goldblum et al. (2024) The No Free Lunch Theorem, Kolmogorov Complexity, and the Role of Inductive Biases (ICML)
finding: Real data is low-complexity, and pre-trained and even randomly initialized GPT-2 models give exponentially higher probability to low-complexity number sequences.
numbers: GPT-3 generates low-complexity sequences with exponentially higher probability; randomly initialized GPT-2 gives a structured distribution; pre-trained checkpoints show a stronger low-complexity preference.
limits: Complexity measured against a chosen reference language on numerical sequences; position paper with small experiments.
agent_relevance: Models already lean toward short rules; the tie-break should not rely on that alone but on held-out checks.

source: Goldblum et al. (2024) The No Free Lunch Theorem, Kolmogorov Complexity (ICML)
finding: Theory: generalization is bounded by training error plus a term in the Kolmogorov complexity K(p) of the model, so simpler fitted hypotheses generalize.
numbers: The bound adds n^-1 (K(p) + 2 log2 K(p) + c) to the cross-entropy (their Eq. 1).
limits: The bound is loose and K is uncomputable; they use network-based upper bounds.
agent_relevance: Formal basis for 'shortest rule that fits' (S7) plus the need for held-out checks.

source: Liao and Gu (2025) ARC-AGI Without Pretraining (CompressARC)
finding: A 76K-parameter network with no pretraining minimizes the description length of the target puzzle at inference time and solves 20% of ARC-AGI-1 evaluation puzzles.
numbers: 20% of evaluation and 34.75% of training puzzles (2 guesses). Baselines in their table: U-Net on target puzzle only 0.75%; HRM-type systems 40.3%; LLM-based systems 87.5% on semi-private eval. About 20 minutes per puzzle on an RTX 4070 (ARC Prize report); 4% on ARC-AGI-2.
quote: to find the shortest possible self-contained program that outputs the entire ARC-AGI dataset
limits: Low absolute score next to LLM systems; compute heavy per puzzle. The ARC-AGI-2 and runtime figures come from a web search summary, not read in full.
agent_relevance: Shows MDL selection of a rule per task works with no pretraining; the agent can copy the idea by preferring the compactest rule that explains all examples.

source: Liao and Gu (2025) ARC-AGI Without Pretraining (CompressARC)
finding: Accuracy on the training set rises with more inference-time steps and with more allowed guesses.
numbers: Appendix table: 100 steps 1.00% in the first column; 500 steps 23.00%; 1000 steps 28.00%; 2000 steps 30.25%; the last column (more guesses) reaches 52.75% at 2000 steps.
limits: Column headings are lost in the extracted text, so the mapping of columns to guess counts is uncertain.
agent_relevance: Compression quality improves smoothly with search budget, so a budget-based stopping rule is natural.

source: Ferre (2025) MADIL: An MDL-based Framework for Efficient Program Synthesis in the ARC Benchmark
finding: A symbolic MDL program-search system (pattern-based task models scored by description length, MCTS search) solves a modest share of ARC.
numbers: 7% at ArcPrize 2024 (private set). On the 400 public evaluation tasks it finds a model correct on all training examples for 69 tasks; 57 are correct on all test examples (82% generalization). 53 of 57 correct on first attempt. 80% of solutions appear in the first 20 s. Correct model sizes 3 to 46, mean 15.2.
limits: Below LLM approaches; the DSL was designed on training tasks only.
agent_relevance: Fit-all-examples then prefer small model generalized at 82%, with an 18% failure rate that held-out checks must catch.

source: Zenil et al. (2026) LLMs are Shannon Lossy Compressors, Not Solomonoff Induction Estimators
finding: Counter-claim: next-token cross-entropy training does not implement Solomonoff induction; models put mass on continuations the declared program class never produces.
numbers: 26 served checkpoints, five families, 0.8-35B parameters, streams from 177,591 programs. None stays within 3.32 bits of a Krichevsky-Trofimov mixture bound; at 24 symbols the best trails by 4.5 bits, the median by 36.5, the worst by 128.
limits: Preprint (v6, Sept 2026); authors promote their own CTM/BDM methods; one specific program class.
agent_relevance: Do not treat LLM likelihood as a clean complexity measure; use executed, verified programs.

source: Zenil et al. (2026) LLMs are Shannon Lossy Compressors, Not Solomonoff Induction Estimators
finding: Describes the Coding Theorem Method and Block Decomposition Method as finite estimators of algorithmic probability, and notes their failure modes.
numbers: No new count; method description. CTM can privilege a short explanation that is wrong, and BDM can obscure structure.
limits: Argument paper; limits stated by the authors.
agent_relevance: A short fit can be wrong: keep held-out checks (G3).

source: Pass (2026) The Value of a Prompt: An LLM-Relative Kolmogorov-Complexity Approach
finding: Defines prompt value as algorithmic mutual information under an LLM-relative probabilistic Levin complexity: b bits of value means the artifact is 2^b times cheaper to obtain.
numbers: Illustration on 12 GSM8K problems with DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B, temperature 0.6, top-p 1, 64 rollouts per problem per condition (with or without the first reference step as a prompt).
limits: The author calls it an illustration, not a population evaluation. Median-based; one small model.
agent_relevance: A way to price a hint or critique in tokens saved; could rank which scaffold step is worth its cost.

source: Shportko (2026) Kolmogorov Complexity Bounds for LLM Steganography and a Perplexity-Based Detection Proxy
finding: Proves hidden-payload embedding raises Kolmogorov complexity by at least |payload| minus O(log n), and uses LM perplexity (Binoculars score) as a computable proxy.
numbers: 300-sample LLM steganographic scheme: paired t = 5.11, p < 1e-6 separating stegotext from baseline.
limits: Preliminary: one scheme, 300 samples.
agent_relevance: Perplexity ratio is a cheap complexity proxy for monitoring agent text.

source: Gauvrit, Zenil, Delahaye, Soler-Toscano (2014) Algorithmic Complexity for Short Binary Strings Applied to Psychology
finding: The Coding Theorem Method gives complexity values for short strings, where ordinary compression fails, to score human randomness production.
numbers: Motivation: Kolmogorov complexity is unusable for strings of length 50 or less; the paper reports a small effect (eta-squared 0.11) in its sample.
limits: Human-side baseline paradigm; only the abstract and parts skimmed.
agent_relevance: Compression fails on short data; use program-count methods for tiny examples such as small grids.

source: Cilibrasi and Vitanyi (2004) Clustering by Compression
finding: Normalized compression distance approximates the uncomputable normalized information distance and clusters genomes, languages and music without features.
numbers: Applied to mammalian mitochondrial genomes (supports Marsupionta over Theria); robust across statistical, dictionary and block-sorting compressors.
limits: Abstract and skim only; later reused for text classification (see Jiang).
agent_relevance: Origin of the compression-distance idea behind gzip-kNN.

source: Cross-reading of Huang 2024, Yoran 2025 and Zenil 2026
finding: Models compress fresh text well and track benchmark skill, yet they find short programs poorly and do not reliably approximate Solomonoff induction.
numbers: Compression-benchmark Pearson -0.93 to -0.95 (Huang) versus GPT4-O program-finding accuracy 6.5% to 35.6% (Yoran).
limits: Synthesis by this agent; different tasks and metrics.
agent_relevance: Use LLM likelihood for ranking; use a program run plus held-out test for selection.

source: Legg and Hutter (2007) Universal Intelligence: A Definition of Machine Intelligence
finding: Defines intelligence as expected performance over all computable environments weighted by 2^-K, so simpler environments count more.
numbers: Formal definition; no experiments. Only the header and keyword lines were seen.
limits: Not read in full; values depend on the reference machine.
agent_relevance: Formal root of weighting simpler rules or environments more.
